## TL;DR

Inventoried every keyboard shortcut the web UI ships, then headless-tested the
command palette and the board navigation against fixtures. Seven real defects
fixed: Escape leaked out of the palette into every window-level handler behind
it (one Esc over an open task drawer closed both), the palette could lose the
z-index tie against an open drawer, a `:focus-visible` rule referenced a custom
property defined nowhere (three dead focus rings), the palette's close button
had no visible focus indicator, the copy-inspector popup's capture-phase
listener leaked Escapes the same way (review round 2), nine more undeclared
custom tokens silently killed text styles, borders and shadows (round 2), and
the palette-vs-confirm-modal stacking is now pinned as deliberate modality
(round 2). Two regression suites (29 jsdom tests + 4 WebKit fixture audits at
375/768/1280) and a QA doc lock it all down.

## Work and rationale

**Inventory first.** I mapped every window/document keydown listener in
`src/ui-app/src`: ⌘K/Ctrl+K palette (SearchBar, with repo/settings delegating to
scoped palettes), the palette's own ↑↓/Enter/Esc/Tab trap, the opt-in board
navigation (j/k/h/l/arrows/Enter/two-stage Esc), settings roving tabs,
Enter-to-send composers, ⌘/Ctrl+Enter form submits, and the Radix drawer's Esc
path. Touch behavior was already right (#1139/#1152): kbd chips and the palette
legend hide on `hover: none`/`pointer: coarse`, the pill becomes a 44×44 icon
button at phone width, and the mobile bar's Search tab opens the palette without
a keyboard. Discoverability is covered by the header chip, the scoped palettes'
chips, the palette footer legend, and the Settings row documenting the board
keys — I verified those rather than adding yet another list.

**The Esc leak was the important find.** radix-vue's drawer honors
`defaultPrevented` on Escape, so I initially expected the layering to be fine —
but the board-nav composable (and HotfixConfirmDialog, DiffView's back
navigation, the deployments confirm, ChatQueuedNotice, MobileTabs' sheet)
listen at window level and don't check it. Fixing at the consumer side would
have meant touching six handlers; fixing at the source — the palette is the
topmost layer while open, so an Esc it handles is *its* Esc — is one
`stopPropagation()` in `SearchOverlay.onKey`, exactly the pattern AreaPicker
already uses. The integration test runs against the real composable: Esc with
the palette over an open drawer closes only the palette; the next Esc closes
the drawer; with the palette closed the two-stage Esc is byte-for-byte the old
behavior.

**Review round 2 added three findings, all fixed.** The copy-inspector popup's
window listener runs in the *capture* phase — it fires before any bubble
handler, so the palette's `stopPropagation` could never reach it, and one Esc
closed the popup plus everything behind it. The handler now consumes the
Escape it acts on and leaves others alone, tested in both directions with a
window-listener spy. The reviewer's edge-case list widened my outline-only
variable guard into a stylesheet-wide one, which flushed out nine more
undeclared tokens (`--txt-muted`, `--txt-secondary`, `--txt-primary`,
`--bg-secondary`, `--border-focus`, `--cyan-border-tint`, `--cyan-tint`,
`--shadow-lg`, `--mono`, bare `var(--font-mono)`) — text meant to be muted was
rendering in the sans face, focus borders and shadows were missing. Rather
than touch ~50 call sites, I declared the aliases once at `:root`: text and
background aliases resolve against the winning theme token, the cyan washes
derive per theme from `--cyan` via `color-mix`, and the mono tokens carry the
canonical JetBrains Mono stack; the light theme gets its own softer
`--shadow-lg`. Runtime-set variables (`--x/--y/--d` from the activity
animation, Vue-bound `--cap-color`) are handled by the guard's definition scan
across all sources, with a documented exception for Radix's own `--radix-*`
popper vars. Finally, the palette-vs-confirm-modal stacking (modals at 1000
and 12000 above the palette at 160) is pinned as deliberate modality by a test
and the ladder comment.

**The z-index tie** (`palette 100 == drawer 100`) I found by walking the
stylesheet's layer ladder; the palette now sits at 160 — above drawers (100),
jump-to-latest (130) and the shot viewer (140/150), below tooltip (200), card
preview (300) and the modal confirmations — with a comment documenting the
ladder, and tests asserting the ordering in both directions by parsing the CSS.

**The dead focus rings** surfaced because my WebKit test asserting the close
button's `:focus-visible` outline kept failing: `.search-overlay-close` had no
ring rule, and while fixing that I noticed three rules using
`var(--focus-ring)` — a variable defined nowhere, so invalid-at-computed-value
time paints nothing. All now use the real `--ring` token.

## Approaches tried

For the WebKit evidence I reused the repo's established split: mount the real
components in jsdom (seeded store + typed query), serialize the rendered
markup, inject it with the real stylesheet, and audit overflow/visibility at
the three QA widths. My first attempt walked Tab to the close button in
WebKit; that fails for a platform reason — macOS WebKit skips buttons on Tab
unless Full Keyboard Access is on — so the Tab-trap assertion moved to jsdom
against the real component and the WebKit test asserts the focus ring the way
`dialog-overlay-browser.test.ts` does (explicit focus + `:focus-visible`).

## Challenges and blockers

- Bare `bunx vitest` doesn't load the Vue plugin; tests must run through
  `bun run test:vitest`. Minor, but cost one false start.
- jsdom lacks `scrollIntoView`; the board nav calls it on every move. Stubbed
  in the suite.
- The gate runs vue-tsc over tests too, which caught a `Ref<boolean>` typing
  nit in my harness on the first check run.
- The capture-phase inspector test needed the same affordance→Enter flow the
  existing component tests use, plus explicit `nextTick`s before asserting
  Vue's DOM updates.

## Key learnings

- When a floating layer consumes a key, consume it completely:
  `preventDefault` alone stops the default action but not sibling
  window-level listeners that implement the same key elsewhere — and a
  capture-phase listener must consume its own keys, because no later handler
  can ever see them stop anything. The repo already knew this (AreaPicker's
  `stopPropagation`, StopWorkConfirmModal's open-stack guard); the palette and
  the copy inspector were the odd ones out.
- CSS custom properties fail silently: `var(--undefined)` computes to
  inherit/initial with no console noise. A source-scan guard is cheap
  insurance, and scoping it to "every fallback-less `var()`" catches far more
  than the single instance that led there.
- Platform behavior differs where you least expect it: headless WebKit tabbing
  to buttons is off by default on macOS. Test the app's trap logic in jsdom,
  keep browser fixtures to layout/visual evidence.

## Verification

`REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passes (build, typecheck, lint, CSS
guards, rendered contrast, scoped tests, WebKit smoke). Suites:
`keyboard-shortcuts-qa.test.ts` (29 jsdom tests) and
`keyboard-shortcuts-qa-browser.test.ts` (4 WebKit fixture audits), plus the
existing `copy-inspector-overlay` and adjacent overlay suites staying green.
QA write-up: `docs/qa/2026-11-keyboard-shortcuts-qa.md`. No `repoos.toml`
change; no runtime dependency; `dist/` untouched.
